## Which test answers the question?

**Use a two-sided paired t test across models for the main comparison.** These
are the same models answering in two languages, rather than separate groups of
English and Chinese models. For each model, calculate its mean reverse-keyed
SDO6 score in each language and compare the 27 Chinese-minus-English differences
with zero. This reproduces the test already quoted in Section 3.2.

A two-way ANOVA is unnecessary for this hypothesis. There is one factor of
interest, language, with two repeated levels. A one-factor repeated-measures
ANOVA on the same model means gives exactly the same result: F = t squared.
A language-by-run ANOVA would additionally ask whether the language difference
varies by run number. Run labels identify replicate sets, not a chronological
sequence for these parallel requests; that interaction is a different question.

**The answer percentages in Fig. 2A are a second question.** A paired t test
tests the mean score, not equality of all seven response frequencies. Below, an
additional test uses Pearson's chi-square statistic but obtains its P value by
swapping the two language profiles within entire models. All items and runs
from a model move together. An ordinary pooled `chisq.test()` P value would
ignore this dependence; `simulate.p.value = TRUE` does not repair it.

The main score test is the existing H1 analysis. The added distribution and
response-feature tests are **exploratory follow-ups**, with Holm adjustment
across those five tests. Do not select a test according to which P value is
smallest.

## Setup and data checks

Run this file with RStudio's **Render** button or, from the repository root:

```bash
quarto render Analysis_script/10_sdo6_language_tests.qmd --output-dir ../Analysis_output/Language_comparison
```

Required packages: `dplyr`, `tidyr`, `readr`, `ggplot2`, and `knitr`.
The file does not install packages or rerun the existing large analysis script.
It reads the August main collection and writes its own results under
`Analysis_output/Language_comparison/`.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
needed <- c("dplyr", "tidyr", "readr", "ggplot2", "knitr")
missing <- needed[!vapply(needed, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing)) {
  stop("Install these R packages before rendering: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "))
}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(readr)
  library(ggplot2)
})

# Locate the project from either the root or the Analysis_script directory.
find_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
  candidate <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
  repeat {
    if (file.exists(file.path(candidate, "Results", "SDO_VSA_Results_20260830.csv"))) {
      return(candidate)
    }
    parent <- dirname(candidate)
    if (identical(parent, candidate)) stop("Cannot locate the main Results folder.")
    candidate <- parent
  }
}
root <- find_root()
out_dir <- file.path(root, "Analysis_output", "Language_comparison")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(20261025)
B_perm <- 99999L
B_boot <- 20000L
options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)

save_csv <- function(x, name) write_csv(x, file.path(out_dir, name))
show_table <- function(x, digits = 4) {
  # Keep small P values visible instead of rounding them to zero in HTML.
  for (name in grep("^p($|_)", names(x), value = TRUE)) {
    if (is.numeric(x[[name]])) x[[name]] <- format.pval(x[[name]], digits = 3, eps = 1e-8)
  }
  knitr::kable(x, digits = digits)
}
p_text <- function(p) {
  if (p < .001) "P < .001" else sprintf("P = %.3f", p)
}
```

The exclusion rule matches the existing script: exclude an endpoint if more
than 50% of its calls in the main attitude collection were API errors.
Non-numeric answers from retained models are missing, never midpoint answers.
The score is recalculated from the original numeric response: items 9-16 are
reverse-keyed as `8 - value`. Thus 1 is most egalitarian and 7 most
hierarchy-endorsing in both languages.

```{r}
#| label: import-and-audit
input_file <- file.path(root, "Results", "SDO_VSA_Results_20260830.csv")
raw <- read_csv(input_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
required <- c("instrument", "language", "model_label", "item_no", "repeat",
              "value", "parse_error", "value_recoded")
stopifnot(all(required %in% names(raw)))

api_audit <- raw |>
  group_by(model_label) |>
  summarise(calls = n(), api_errors = sum(parse_error == "API_ERROR", na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(api_error_share = api_errors / calls,
         excluded = api_error_share > .50)
excluded_models <- api_audit |> filter(excluded)
save_csv(api_audit, "endpoint_exclusion_audit.csv")
show_table(excluded_models)

sdo6 <- raw |>
  filter(instrument == "SDO6", !model_label %in% excluded_models$model_label) |>
  mutate(run = as.integer(.data[["repeat"]]) + 1L,
         item_no = as.integer(item_no),
         score = if_else(item_no >= 9L, 8 - value, value))

# Stop on duplicate calls or unexpected scale values instead of averaging them.
stopifnot(all(sdo6$language %in% c("en", "zh")),
          all(sdo6$item_no %in% 1:16), all(sdo6$run %in% 1:5),
          all(is.na(sdo6$score) | sdo6$score %in% 1:7))
duplicates <- sdo6 |> count(model_label, language, item_no, run) |> filter(n != 1L)
stopifnot(nrow(duplicates) == 0L)
design <- sdo6 |> count(model_label, language, name = "attempts")
stopifnot(all(design$attempts == 80L), nrow(design) == 2L * n_distinct(sdo6$model_label))
key_check <- sdo6 |> filter(!is.na(score), !is.na(value_recoded))
stopifnot(all(key_check$score == key_check$value_recoded))

audit <- sdo6 |>
  group_by(language) |>
  summarise(models = n_distinct(model_label), attempts = n(),
            valid_answers = sum(!is.na(score)),
            missing_answers = sum(is.na(score)),
            pooled_mean = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
save_csv(audit, "data_audit.csv")
show_table(audit)
```

There are `r sum(audit$attempts)` attempted SDO6 answers and
`r sum(audit$valid_answers)` numeric answers. Missing answers include refusals
and other unparseable responses; these counts are not refusal counts.
All analyses below condition on having a numeric answer. They do not establish
what the missing answers would have been.

## Main test: mean SDO6 scores

For continuity with the existing manuscript analysis, first average all available
numeric answers within each model and language. Each model then contributes
exactly one paired difference and receives equal weight. The five runs and
16 items improve each score's measurement; they do not increase the number of
independent models from 27 to thousands.

```{r}
#| label: paired-score-test
model_scores <- sdo6 |>
  group_by(model_label, language) |>
  summarise(mean_score = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_valid = sum(!is.na(score)), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = language, values_from = c(mean_score, n_valid)) |>
  mutate(difference = mean_score_zh - mean_score_en)
stopifnot(all(is.finite(model_scores$difference)))

paired_test <- t.test(model_scores$mean_score_zh, model_scores$mean_score_en,
                      paired = TRUE, alternative = "two.sided", conf.level = .95)
primary <- tibble(
  analysis = "Available-answer model means (primary)",
  n_models = nrow(model_scores),
  mean_en = mean(model_scores$mean_score_en),
  mean_zh = mean(model_scores$mean_score_zh),
  difference_zh_minus_en = mean(model_scores$difference),
  ci_low = paired_test$conf.int[1], ci_high = paired_test$conf.int[2],
  t = unname(paired_test$statistic), df = unname(paired_test$parameter),
  p = paired_test$p.value,
  cohens_dz = mean(model_scores$difference) / sd(model_scores$difference),
  higher_in_zh = sum(round(model_scores$difference, 10) > 0),
  higher_in_en = sum(round(model_scores$difference, 10) < 0)
)
save_csv(model_scores, "scores_by_model.csv")
save_csv(primary, "primary_paired_t_test.csv")
show_table(primary |> transmute(
  Models = n_models, English = mean_en, Chinese = mean_zh,
  Difference = difference_zh_minus_en,
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", ci_low, ci_high),
  `t (df)` = sprintf("%.2f (%d)", t, df), p = p))
```

The model-weighted mean difference is **`r sprintf("%.3f", primary$difference_zh_minus_en)`
scale points**, 95% CI [`r sprintf("%.3f", primary$ci_low)`,
`r sprintf("%.3f", primary$ci_high)`], t(`r primary$df`) =
`r sprintf("%.2f", primary$t)`, `r p_text(primary$p)`.
The pooled answer means and the means of model means are slightly different
quantities when models have different numbers of valid answers. The paired
test uses model means, not the two pooled means.

### Check against repeated-measures ANOVA

```{r}
#| label: anova-equivalence
anova_data <- model_scores |>
  select(model_label, mean_score_en, mean_score_zh) |>
  pivot_longer(starts_with("mean_score_"), names_to = "language", values_to = "score") |>
  mutate(model_label = factor(model_label), language = factor(language))
one_way_rm <- aov(score ~ language + Error(model_label / language), data = anova_data)
anova_table <- summary(one_way_rm)[["Error: model_label:language"]][[1]]
anova_check <- tibble(
  F = anova_table["language", "F value"], t_squared = primary$t^2,
  df1 = anova_table["language", "Df"], df2 = anova_table["Residuals", "Df"],
  p_anova = anova_table["language", "Pr(>F)"], p_paired_t = primary$p)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(anova_check$F, anova_check$t_squared, tolerance = 1e-8)))
save_csv(anova_check, "one_factor_rm_anova_equivalence.csv")
show_table(anova_check)
```

### Robustness and missing-answer checks

The exact sign test asks whether more than half of the non-tied model differences
are positive. It does not require normally distributed differences. It tests a
directional tendency across models, rather than the mean difference itself.

```{r}
#| label: sign-and-sensitivity
nonzero <- round(model_scores$difference, 10)
nonzero <- nonzero[nonzero != 0]
sign_test <- binom.test(sum(nonzero > 0), length(nonzero), p = .5,
                       alternative = "two.sided")
sign_result <- tibble(n_nonzero = length(nonzero), positive = sum(nonzero > 0),
                      negative = sum(nonzero < 0), p = sign_test$p.value)
save_csv(sign_result, "exact_sign_test.csv")
show_table(sign_result)

# Match numeric answers on model, item and replicate label. This is a
# completeness restriction, not a claim of time-matched or seeded requests.
paired_answers <- sdo6 |>
  select(model_label, item_no, run, language, score) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = language, values_from = score) |>
  filter(!is.na(en), !is.na(zh))
pair_audit <- paired_answers |> count(model_label, name = "complete_pairs")
save_csv(pair_audit, "complete_pairs_by_model.csv")

complete_scores <- paired_answers |>
  group_by(model_label) |>
  summarise(en = mean(en), zh = mean(zh), .groups = "drop")

# Equal item weights are a separate check when different items have different
# numbers of valid repeats.
equal_item_scores <- sdo6 |>
  group_by(model_label, language, item_no) |>
  summarise(item_mean = mean(score, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(is.finite(item_mean)) |>
  group_by(model_label, language) |>
  summarise(score = mean(item_mean), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = language, values_from = score)

paired_summary <- function(data, label) {
  fit <- t.test(data$zh, data$en, paired = TRUE)
  tibble(analysis = label, n_models = nrow(data),
         difference = mean(data$zh - data$en),
         ci_low = fit$conf.int[1], ci_high = fit$conf.int[2],
         t = unname(fit$statistic), df = unname(fit$parameter), p = fit$p.value)
}
sensitivity <- bind_rows(
  paired_summary(complete_scores, "Only model-item-run pairs numeric in both languages"),
  paired_summary(equal_item_scores, "Equal item weights after averaging repeats"),
  paired_summary(model_scores |>
    filter(model_label != "databricks-meta-llama-3-1-8b-instruct") |>
    transmute(en = mean_score_en, zh = mean_score_zh),
    "Primary scoring, excluding Llama 3.1 8B")
)
save_csv(sensitivity, "score_sensitivity_checks.csv")
show_table(sensitivity)
```

These are robustness checks on the same hypothesis, not additional independent
replications. All confidence intervals here are pointwise 95% intervals.

## Fig. 2A: do the answer distributions differ?

First reproduce the descriptive distribution using all available numeric
answers. The denominator is the number of numeric answers in that language,
not all attempted calls.

```{r}
#| label: answer-distribution
distribution <- sdo6 |>
  filter(!is.na(score)) |>
  count(language, score, name = "n") |>
  complete(language = c("en", "zh"), score = 1:7, fill = list(n = 0L)) |>
  group_by(language) |>
  mutate(percent = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()
save_csv(distribution, "all_valid_answer_distribution.csv")
show_table(distribution, digits = 2)

ggplot(distribution, aes(factor(score), percent, fill = language)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge", width = .8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(en = "#2878A5", zh = "#CF683D"),
                    labels = c(en = "English", zh = "Chinese")) +
  labs(x = "Reverse-keyed SDO6 answer (1 = most egalitarian)",
       y = "Numeric answers (%)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Chi-square statistic with model-level language swaps

To give the two languages identical item/run coverage, restrict this additional
test to the **`r nrow(paired_answers)` complete pairs**. Within each model,
count the answers at each of the seven scale points in each language. On every
permutation, independently decide for each model whether to swap its **entire**
English and Chinese profiles, retaining all dependence among its items and
runs. Use `r format(B_perm, big.mark = ",")` random swaps with a fixed seed.

For equal row totals, Pearson's statistic can be calculated as
sum over categories of `(Chinese count - English count)^2 / combined count`.
The code uses that identity for speed. Its P value comes from the model-level
permutation distribution, **not a chi-square reference distribution with six
degrees of freedom**. It is an omnibus test: a significant result establishes a
distribution difference, not its direction.

This procedure assumes that, under the null, each model's two complete language
profiles are exchangeable and swaps can be chosen independently across models.
It conditions on the fixed 16 items and complete numeric pairs. Missingness
depending on language can still bias a complete-pair comparison. Related model
families may also violate independence across endpoints; the test does not
justify inference to all possible LLMs or all possible questionnaire items.

```{r}
#| label: clustered-distribution-test
models <- sort(unique(paired_answers$model_label))
M <- length(models)
en_counts <- t(vapply(models, function(m) {
  tabulate(as.integer(paired_answers$en[paired_answers$model_label == m]), nbins = 7L)
}, integer(7)))
zh_counts <- t(vapply(models, function(m) {
  tabulate(as.integer(paired_answers$zh[paired_answers$model_label == m]), nbins = 7L)
}, integer(7)))
stopifnot(all(rowSums(en_counts) == rowSums(zh_counts)))
dimnames(en_counts) <- dimnames(zh_counts) <- list(models, as.character(1:7))
category_totals <- colSums(en_counts + zh_counts)
present <- category_totals > 0
count_differences <- zh_counts[, present, drop = FALSE] -
                     en_counts[, present, drop = FALSE]
observed_x2 <- sum(colSums(count_differences)^2 / category_totals[present])

# Verify the statistic against R, but deliberately do not use its pooled P value.
pooled_table <- rbind(en = colSums(en_counts), zh = colSums(zh_counts))[, present]
reference_stat <- suppressWarnings(chisq.test(pooled_table, correct = FALSE)$statistic)
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(observed_x2, unname(reference_stat), tolerance = 1e-8)))

# One sign per model per permutation; all of its answers move together.
set.seed(20261025)
swaps <- matrix(sample(c(-1, 1), B_perm * M, replace = TRUE), nrow = B_perm, ncol = M)
permuted_count_differences <- swaps %*% count_differences
permuted_x2 <- rowSums(sweep(permuted_count_differences^2, 2,
                            category_totals[present], FUN = "/"))
exceedances <- sum(permuted_x2 >= observed_x2 - 1e-10)
omnibus_p <- (exceedances + 1) / (B_perm + 1)
omnibus <- tibble(test = "Seven-category distribution: model-level swaps",
                  complete_pairs = nrow(paired_answers), n_models = M,
                  pearson_x2_statistic = observed_x2, permutations = B_perm,
                  exceedances = exceedances, p = omnibus_p,
                  monte_carlo_se_approx = sqrt(omnibus_p * (1 - omnibus_p) / (B_perm + 1)))
save_csv(as.data.frame(as.table(pooled_table)), "complete_pair_distribution_counts.csv")
show_table(omnibus |> select(-test, -monte_carlo_se_approx))
```

### Which features changed?

Four follow-ups describe the interpretation in Section 3.2: choosing the most
egalitarian option (1), using either endpoint (1 or 7), mean distance from the
midpoint (`abs(score - 4)`), and choosing the hierarchy-endorsing side (5-7).
For each model, calculate these summaries on the same complete pairs and then
average their Chinese-minus-English differences across models. A negative
endpoint or distance difference indicates less extreme responding in Chinese.

Two-sided permutation P values use the same whole-model swaps. A bootstrap
resamples entire models, preserving each English/Chinese pair, for basic
bootstrap pointwise 95% confidence intervals. Proportion effects and their intervals are converted
to percentage points. The Holm family contains the omnibus test plus these
four follow-ups. It does not retrospectively replace the manuscript's existing
multiple-testing registry.

```{r}
#| label: response-feature-tests
features <- list(
  most_egalitarian_option = function(x) as.numeric(x == 1),
  either_endpoint = function(x) as.numeric(x %in% c(1, 7)),
  distance_from_midpoint = function(x) abs(x - 4),
  hierarchy_endorsing_side = function(x) as.numeric(x >= 5)
)
feature_data <- lapply(names(features), function(name) {
  f <- features[[name]]
  paired_answers |>
    group_by(model_label) |>
    summarise(en = mean(f(en)), zh = mean(f(zh)), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(feature = name, difference = zh - en) |>
    arrange(match(model_label, models))
})
names(feature_data) <- names(features)
set.seed(20261026)
boot_index <- matrix(sample.int(M, B_boot * M, replace = TRUE), nrow = B_boot, ncol = M)

feature_results <- bind_rows(lapply(names(feature_data), function(name) {
  d <- feature_data[[name]]
  delta <- d$difference
  stopifnot(identical(d$model_label, models))
  estimate <- mean(delta)
  permuted <- drop(swaps %*% delta) / M
  p <- (1 + sum(abs(permuted) >= abs(estimate) - 1e-12)) / (B_perm + 1)
  boot_means <- rowMeans(matrix(delta[boot_index], nrow = B_boot, ncol = M))
  # Basic bootstrap interval: reflect the bootstrap quantiles around the estimate.
  ci <- 2 * estimate - unname(quantile(boot_means, c(.975, .025)))
  multiplier <- if (name == "distance_from_midpoint") 1 else 100
  tibble(feature = name,
         unit = if (multiplier == 100) "percentage points" else "scale points",
         mean_en = multiplier * mean(d$en), mean_zh = multiplier * mean(d$zh),
         difference_zh_minus_en = multiplier * estimate,
         ci_low = multiplier * ci[1], ci_high = multiplier * ci[2], p = p)
}))
adjusted <- p.adjust(c(omnibus$p, feature_results$p), method = "holm")
omnibus$p_holm <- adjusted[1]
feature_results$p_holm <- adjusted[-1]
save_csv(omnibus, "clustered_distribution_test.csv")
save_csv(feature_results, "response_feature_tests.csv")
save_csv(bind_rows(feature_data), "response_features_by_model.csv")
show_table(feature_results |> transmute(
  Feature = recode(feature,
    most_egalitarian_option = "Most egalitarian option (%)",
    either_endpoint = "Either endpoint (%)",
    distance_from_midpoint = "Distance from midpoint (points)",
    hierarchy_endorsing_side = "Hierarchy-endorsing side (%)"),
  English = mean_en, Chinese = mean_zh, `ZH - EN` = difference_zh_minus_en,
  `95% CI` = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", ci_low, ci_high), p = p, p_holm = p_holm),
  digits = 2)
```

An insignificant hierarchy-side comparison would **not** establish equivalence
between languages. Describe those responses as rare if the percentages support
that statement; do not write that they are statistically unchanged without a
separately justified equivalence margin and test. Likewise, an aggregate shift
does not imply that every model/item pair stayed on the same side.

## Suggested reporting

The following sentences are generated from this run. The first reports the
existing score hypothesis; the second addresses the added Fig. 2A test.

```{r}
#| label: reporting-text
#| results: asis
main_sentence <- sprintf(
  paste0("SDO6 scores were higher in Chinese than in English for %d of %d models. ",
         "The mean within-model difference was %.2f scale points (Chinese minus English; ",
         "95%% CI [%.2f, %.2f]; two-sided paired t test across models, t(%d) = %.2f, %s)."),
  primary$higher_in_zh, primary$n_models, primary$difference_zh_minus_en,
  primary$ci_low, primary$ci_high, primary$df, primary$t, p_text(primary$p))
distribution_sentence <- sprintf(
  paste0("In an exploratory comparison restricted to %s model-item-run pairs with numeric ",
         "answers in both languages, the seven-category response distributions %s ",
         "(Pearson chi-square statistic = %.2f; %s permutations swapping entire language ",
         "profiles within models; unadjusted %s; Holm-adjusted %s across five follow-up tests)."),
  format(nrow(paired_answers), big.mark = ","),
  if (omnibus$p_holm < .05) "differed" else "did not differ significantly",
  omnibus$pearson_x2_statistic, format(B_perm, big.mark = ","),
  p_text(omnibus$p), p_text(omnibus$p_holm))
reporting_text <- c(main_sentence, "", distribution_sentence, "",
  paste0("Interpretation: the mean score comparison concerns these tested model endpoints ",
         "and these two SDO6 versions. A language-version difference alone cannot distinguish ",
         "response style, translation/label effects, or an attitude difference."))
writeLines(reporting_text, file.path(out_dir, "suggested_results_text.txt"))
cat(paste(reporting_text, collapse = "\n\n"))
```

The score test already supplies statistical support for a lower English SDO6
score. Prefer **"the models gave more egalitarian responses in English"** to a
claim about an intrinsic attitude. Only one Chinese translation was tested.

The supplied supplementary information already reports the paired score test
in Supplementary Table S4, together with analyses of distance from the midpoint
and endpoint responding. The present notebook reproduces the score comparison
from the raw data and adds a direct seven-category distribution comparison.
Its new follow-up tests use complete run/item pairs and whole-model swaps,
so they need not numerically match those earlier analyses.

## Assumptions and reproducibility

- The paired t test assumes independent model differences and approximately
  normal sampling behavior for their mean. The sign test and complete-pair
  distribution test provide complementary checks with different null hypotheses.
- The endpoints were selected rather than randomly sampled. Models from the
  same developer may be related. Report the result for this tested set; these
  analyses do not model dependence between related endpoints.
- Items and language versions are fixed here. Generalizing to a population of
  items would require an appropriate crossed model and measurement assumptions.
- The runs are replicate labels, not paired random seeds or matched time points.
- A change in observed scale scores is not sufficient evidence that the latent
  attitude is measured equivalently across the two versions.
- The permutation P values include the observed configuration through the
  `(exceedances + 1)/(B + 1)` correction and are never reported as zero.
- The bootstrap intervals are pointwise, not simultaneous intervals. Follow-up
  conclusions use the Holm-adjusted P values in the exported tables.

Method references: [R paired t-test documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/t.test.html),
[R chi-square documentation](https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/stats/html/chisq.test.html),
and [Winkler et al. (2014), permutation inference and exchangeability blocks](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuroimage.2014.01.060).

```{r}
#| label: reproducibility
#| echo: false
provenance <- tibble(input = "Results/SDO_VSA_Results_20260830.csv",
                     md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_file)),
                     permutation_seed = 20261025L, bootstrap_seed = 20261026L,
                     permutations = B_perm, bootstrap_resamples = B_boot)
save_csv(provenance, "analysis_provenance.csv")
capture.output(sessionInfo(), file = file.path(out_dir, "sessionInfo.txt"))
show_table(provenance)
sessionInfo()
```
